files.content:
# Future Considerations for the Todo List Application

## Potential Features

The Todo list application may evolve to incorporate features designed to meet a wider range of user needs, improve engagement, strengthen retention, and ensure competitiveness as user expectations increase. These features are not part of the minimum viable product but are considered for future planning and should be kept in scope for business and technical evaluation.

### User Experience Enhancements
- WHEN users have complex tasks, THE system SHALL support subtasks or nested todos to break down larger goals.
- WHEN users desire to manage priorities, THE system SHALL provide options for marking todos as low, medium, high, or urgent.
- WHEN a user wants to track deadlines, THE system SHALL allow due dates with notification or reminder mechanisms that alert users appropriately using email or push methods.
- WHEN a task needs to be performed repeatedly, THE system SHALL allow users to easily set tasks as recurring at daily, weekly, or custom intervals.
- WHEN users want richer context, THE system SHALL support attaching images, documents, or URLs to individual todos, preserving security and privacy.
- IF users desire to organize tasks flexibly, THEN THE system SHALL enable custom labels or tags for categorization, filtering, and user-defined views.

### Collaboration and Sharing
- WHEN users need to coordinate with others (e.g., families, teams, groups), THE system SHALL support shared todo lists where multiple users may view and contribute tasks.
- WHEN shared lists are enabled, THE system SHALL enforce permission controls via user roles, such as viewer and editor, to avoid unauthorized changes.
- WHEN task collaboration occurs, THE system SHALL maintain an activity history to track all changes and updates, creating audit trails and accountability.
- WHEN teams require communication on tasks, THE system SHALL enable comments and notes to be added within any todo for richer context.

### Integrations and Extensibility
- IF users want to sync with external tools, THEN THE system SHALL offer calendar integration, allowing due dates to appear on common services (Google, Outlook, etc.).
- WHEN users adopt other productivity platforms, THE system SHALL provide mechanisms for importing and exporting tasks using industry-standard APIs.
- WHERE timely task status is critical, THE system SHALL offer mobile push notifications for reminders and updates.
- IF users want to interact hands-free, THEN THE system SHALL provide voice assistant integration for task add/view actions.
- WHEN organizations require process automation, THE system SHALL allow for integration with platforms such as Zapier or IFTTT, triggering third-party actions on todo changes.

### Personalization and Advanced Features
- IF users seek a customized experience, THEN THE system SHALL provide theming options including light/dark mode and high-contrast accessibility.
- WHEN users want insights into productivity, THE system SHALL provide analytics such as task completion rates, overdue trends, and activity summaries.
- IF accidental deletion occurs, THEN THE system SHALL maintain an archive/trash feature, allowing restoration of todos for a period before permanent removal.
- WHERE common workflows exist, THE system SHALL provide reusable templates and checklists.
- IF engagement is a business goal, THEN THE system MAY implement gamification (badges, streaks, points) to motivate frequent use.

### Security and Data Privacy
- WHEN user accounts need greater security, THE system SHALL provide multi-factor authentication options.
- WHEN data portability is requested, THE system SHALL support secure data export and import options for user backup and transfer.
- WHEN users need privacy for sensitive information, THE system SHALL implement end-to-end encryption of todo data.

## Scaling Considerations

### User Base Growth
- WHEN the number of registered users increases beyond projections, THE system SHALL maintain application responsiveness and user experience with predictable performance.
- IF daily active user numbers spike due to promotions, THEN THE system SHALL scale horizontally and vertically (application servers, database, storage) to handle increased load and data volume.

### Data Management
- WHEN users create a large number of todos or attachments, THE system SHALL provide efficient storage management with pagination, data archiving, and resource optimization.
- IF collaborative lists reach large participant counts, THEN THE system SHALL implement scalable access control, ensuring permission checks remain performant as group size increases.

### Operational and Technical Scalability
- IF infrastructure limitations are reached, THEN THE system SHALL support seamless deployment to higher-capacity environments or cloud providers.
- WHEN business operations demand monitoring, THE system SHALL expose metrics (performance, error rates) to proactively detect and resolve issues before user impact.
- IF a disaster recovery requirement exists, THEN THE system SHALL support regular secure backups, quick restore procedures, and transparent communication of issues.
- WHEN expanding regionally or adopting multi-tenancy models, THE system SHALL ensure strict isolation and data segregation between organizational units to protect privacy and compliance.

## Long-term Vision

### Business Evolution
- WHEN the todo platform achieves a large and loyal user base, THE business SHALL evaluate monetization strategies, including premium features, subscriptions, and enterprise solutions for organizations.
- IF complementary productivity services align with market strategy, THEN THE service SHALL initiate integration partnerships to augment user capabilities and drive organic growth.

### Feature and Technology Strategy
- WHERE user research or emerging trends suggest unmet needs, THE system roadmap SHALL prioritize features that directly contribute to user engagement, retention, and satisfaction.
- THROUGHOUT ongoing development, THE system SHALL preserve commitments to simplicity, reliability, fast performance, and a positive user experience even as feature depth increases.
- THE product lifecycle SHALL integrate regular user feedback for continuous improvement, ensuring business relevance and competitive advantage.

### Roadmap for Ecosystem Expansion
- WHERE new opportunities are validated, THE todo platform MAY extend into habit tracking, project management, calendar features, or advanced team collaboration (permissions, roles, automation).
- THE architecture SHALL remain modular and API-driven to enable future feature additions, third-party integrations, and a broader productivity ecosystem.

## Mermaid Diagram: Future Expansion Paths

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Basic Todo App"] --> B["User Experience Enhancements"]
  A --> C["Collaboration & Sharing"]
  A --> D["Integrations"]
  B --> E["Subtasks & Priority"]
  B --> F["Reminders & Recurrence"]
  C --> G["Shared Lists"]
  C --> H["Role-based Permissions"]
  D --> I["Calendar Sync"]
  D --> J["API Access"]
  D --> K["Automation"]
  K --> L["Third-Party Plugins"]
  B --> M["Personalization & Analytics"]
  D --> N["Smart Assistant Integration"]
  C --> O["Comments & Activity Log"]
```

models.name: todo_users
models.description:
Registered users for the Todo List application. 

Represents all individual identities authorized to use the system. Each user is uniquely identified by their email address and can manage their own personal todos, but is strictly isolated from all other users by access controls and permissions. Passwords are securely stored using strong hash algorithms; no plain-text credentials are ever retained.

User accounts cannot access or modify any other user's data. All authentication flows, session establishment, and permission checks depend primarily on this table.

Timestamps enable tracking of account creation and the last time credentials or user records were modified. No administrative users or privileged roles exist in this MVP.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Universally unique user identifier for each application user. Must not collide with any other id in the system.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: The user's unique email address. Used for authentication and business communication. Must be unique among all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for user authentication. Never stores the plain-text password. Follows industry-standard secure hash algorithm requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the user account was initially created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the user's account information (such as password or email).

models.name: todo_user_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for users of the Todo List application.

Each record represents a single authenticated session established by a user. Sessions are created at user login, persist throughout authenticated API usage, and are invalidated at logout or expiration. The session is always linked to exactly one user.

Sessions record connection context (IP, href, referrer) and temporal data (creation and expiration times). Session records enable audit trails for security and troubleshooting. Sessions are strictly subsidiary to their parent user, managed through identity flows, and are never edited directly except by system actions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Universally unique session identifier for each authentication/session instance.

foreignFields.name: todo_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the user who owns this session. Establishes the relationship with {@link todo_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was established. Used for auditing and security context.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL where the session started (landing or login page). Captures the source for audit and analytics.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL for the session, providing additional context to the authentication attempt.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was invalidated. Null if the session is still active.

models.name: todo_todos
models.description:
Todo items for individual users.

This table stores all todo entries created by users. Each todo is strictly owned by a single user, represented by a foreign key reference to the {@link todo_users} table. The model enforces field level constraints per requirements: 'title' is always required (1-255 char), 'description' is optional (up to 1000 chars), and 'status' can only be 'complete' or 'incomplete'. Each todo includes timestamps for creation, last update, and (optionally) completion to support rapid lookup, sorting, and user-facing status. This model provides strong ownership enforcement—no sharing, delegation, or multi-user association is possible. All CRUD operations are limited to the owning user. Hard deletes (no deleted_at) are specified per business requirement. All business, validation, and ownership rules are enforced at the schema and API layers.

foreignFields.name: todo_user_id
foreignFields.description: Owner of this todo, referencing a registered user. Foreign key to {@link todo_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Todo title (1-255 characters). Required at all times.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Completion status; allowed values are 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Only these two string values are valid.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when todo was marked as complete (UTC, ISO8601). Null if incomplete.

models._comment_fields_constraints: Enforcement of allowed values (status: 'incomplete' | 'complete') and length constraints (title ≤255, description ≤1000) should be implemented at API/service validation and reflected in database if possible.

### `todo_users`

Registered users for the Todo List application.

Represents all individual identities authorized to use the system. Each
user is uniquely identified by their email address and can manage their
own personal todos, but is strictly isolated from all other users by
access controls and permissions. Passwords are securely stored using
strong hash algorithms; no plain-text credentials are ever retained.

User accounts cannot access or modify any other user's data. All
authentication flows, session establishment, and permission checks depend
primarily on this table.

Timestamps enable tracking of account creation and the last time
credentials or user records were modified. No administrative users or
privileged roles exist in this MVP.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > Primary Key. Universally unique user identifier for each application
  > user. Must not collide with any other id in the system.
- `email`
  > The user's unique email address. Used for authentication and business
  > communication. Must be unique among all users.
- `password_hash`
  > Hashed password for user authentication. Never stores the plain-text
  > password. Follows industry-standard secure hash algorithm requirements.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the user account was initially created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of the most recent update to the user's account information
  > (such as password or email).

### `todo_user_sessions`

Authentication sessions for users of the Todo List application.

Each record represents a single authenticated session established by a
user. Sessions are created at user login, persist throughout
authenticated API usage, and are invalidated at logout or expiration. The
session is always linked to exactly one user.

Sessions record connection context (IP, href, referrer) and temporal data
(creation and expiration times). Session records enable audit trails for
security and troubleshooting. Sessions are strictly subsidiary to their
parent user, managed through identity flows, and are never edited
directly except by system actions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > Primary Key. Universally unique session identifier for each
  > authentication/session instance.
- `todo_user_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the user who owns this session. Establishes the
  > relationship with [todo_users.id](#todo_users).
- `ip`
  > IP address from which the session was established. Used for auditing and
  > security context.
- `href`
  > Full URL where the session started (landing or login page). Captures the
  > source for audit and analytics.
- `referrer`
  > Referrer URL for the session, providing additional context to the
  > authentication attempt.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the session expired or was invalidated. Null if the
  > session is still active.

## Todos

```mermaid
erDiagram
"todo_todos" {
  String id PK
  String todo_user_id FK
  String title
  String description "nullable"
  String status
  DateTime created_at
  DateTime updated_at
  DateTime completed_at "nullable"
}
```

### `todo_todos`

Todo items for individual users.

This table stores all todo entries created by users. Each todo is
strictly owned by a single user, represented by a foreign key reference
to the [todo_users](#todo_users) table. The model enforces field level
constraints per requirements: 'title' is always required (1-255 char),
'description' is optional (up to 1000 chars), and 'status' can only be
'complete' or 'incomplete'. Each todo includes timestamps for creation,
last update, and (optionally) completion to support rapid lookup,
sorting, and user-facing status. This model provides strong ownership
enforcement—no sharing, delegation, or multi-user association is
possible. All CRUD operations are limited to the owning user. Hard
deletes (no deleted_at) are specified per business requirement. All
business, validation, and ownership rules are enforced at the schema and
API layers.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_user_id`
  > Owner of this todo, referencing a registered user. Foreign key to {@link
  > todo_users.id}.
- `title`: Todo title (1-255 characters). Required at all times.
- `description`: Optional description with maximum 1000 characters.
- `status`
  > Completion status; allowed values are 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Only
  > these two string values are valid.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of todo creation (UTC, ISO8601).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last modification (UTC, ISO8601).
- `completed_at`
  > Timestamp when todo was marked as complete (UTC, ISO8601). Null if
  > incomplete.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full detail for a single authentication session belonging to a specific user, based on the unique sessionId and parent userId (UUIDs) as defined in the todo_users and todo_user_sessions tables. It allows authorized actors to conduct security reviews or forensic analysis on a particular authentication event, providing context such as session origination, timing, and referrer details.

Only read-only access is permitted, enabling safe auditing of session histories. The endpoint enforces ownership by requiring both userId (parent context) and sessionId (session identifier), in line with the strict parent-child relationship in the schema. The operation is essential for compliance, troubleshooting, and security investigations. The session is not editable or deletable by API. Session establishment and termination are managed exclusively by authentication mechanisms outside the API surface, reflecting strong business controls on session lifecycles. Related operations include session history retrieval for the user.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full technical and business details for a single authentication session belonging to a given user in the Todo List application.

This operation is designed for security, compliance, and forensic analysis, returning all session-related fields including connection context, creation and (if expired) expiration time, user association, and audit metadata. Session establishment or termination is managed by privileged authentication flows, not by this API.

Both path parameters must match (userId for parent user, sessionId for session record), with comprehensive access controls enforced for privacy reasons. This endpoint cannot be used to edit or delete session data.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed data of a specific authentication session for a user (todo_user_sessions table)

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent user for this session (UUID as per todo_users.id)

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique session identifier of the authentication session record (UUID as per todo_user_sessions.id)

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the specific user authentication session record

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation deletes a specific user session by session ID, removing authentication and effectively logging out the user from that session. It targets the subsidiary 'todo_user_sessions' Prisma DB table, which stores each authenticated session with information about the linked user, context, and validity. Deleting a session is equivalent to an explicit logout request and ensures that the target session is no longer valid for authenticated API calls. Only the session owner (authenticated user) is permitted to delete their own session, preventing any possibility of terminating other users' sessions. The operation checks strict ownership based on both userId and sessionId to enforce account security. Hard deletion is used (no soft delete), as specified in the schema and requirements. Audit logging and immediate token invalidation are handled by the provider/business logic layer.
operations.description:
Delete a single user session, terminating the current authenticated context for the requesting user.

This API operation requires both the user ID and the session ID as path parameters. It ensures that only the user who owns the session can delete (invalidate) their own session, following strict ownership and isolation rules for security. If the provided IDs do not correspond to a valid session owned by the user, the operation returns a clear error indicating unauthorized access or resource not found.

No request body is required. The operation permanently removes the session from the database (no soft-deletion); once deleted, all further API requests using this session are immediately denied. This supports secure logout flows and session management, in full compliance with requirements for user isolation and auditability.

This operation is related to session management features, and pairs with provider logic to revoke tokens and log authentication events. Other API endpoints requiring authentication must always verify session validity.
operations.summary: Remove an authenticated user's session (logout) in the 'todo_user_sessions' table by sessionId and userId.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user who owns the session (must match the authenticated user).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session to be deleted (from 'todo_user_sessions' table).

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of todos belonging to the authenticated user, supporting advanced search by title, description, and status, along with robust sorting and pagination. The underlying database model is the 'todo_todos' Prisma table, which enforces ownership, validation, and constraints on every todo item (e.g., required title 1-255 chars, optional description up to 1000 chars, status 'complete' or 'incomplete'). The API returns only those todos associated with the authenticated user, strictly excluding all others by design. This operation implements all business requirements for list and search, supporting default and custom sort orders, filters by status, and text search as permitted by schema and indexes.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a personalized, paginated list of todo items belonging to the authenticated user in the Todo List application.

This endpoint enables users to filter todos by completion status ('complete' or 'incomplete'), partial matches in title or description, and sort results as desired. Pagination and sorting help users efficiently manage large todo lists. Security, privacy, and ownership are strictly enforced: only todos created by the authenticated user are accessible. Attempts to search for todos of other users will always return empty result sets and do not leak resource existence information.

Validation rules (as per schema) apply to every field: titles must be 1-255 characters, descriptions up to 1000 characters if present, and status must be 'complete' or 'incomplete'. The response structure follows best practices for API search—users receive summary information suitable for listing, with detailed fields available in separate detail queries if required. All query behaviors match non-functional and business criteria described in requirements.
operations.summary: Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of todos for the authenticated user from the 'todo_todos' table.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for retrieving the user's todos; supports filtering by status, title, description, and custom sort/pagination options.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summary objects matching the search and filter criteria, belonging only to the authenticated user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information for a specific todo item owned by a user. It accesses the todo_todos Prisma table, utilizing its strict ownership model to ensure that each todo is associated with exactly one user. The todo entry is identified by its globally unique UUID. All relevant fields, including title, description, status, creation and update timestamps, and (optionally) completed_at, are returned. The todo_user_id foreign key enforces that only the owning user may access this todo item.
operations.description:
Fetch details for a specific todo item.

This operation returns all persisted information for the designated todo item, as defined in the todo_todos table. Users must supply the unique identifier of the target todo via path parameter. Returned data includes the todo's required title (1-255 characters), optional description (up to 1000 characters), status (only 'complete' or 'incomplete' allowed), timestamps for creation, last update, and (if applicable) completion.

Security: Only the owning user (as specified by todo_user_id foreign key) can access this resource. No sharing or delegation is possible under current business and schema rules. Attempts by any other user will result in an authorization error.

The implementation must strictly enforce validation, field access, and error handling in accordance with the table's schema-level comments. Related operations include creation, editing (PUT), and deletion (DELETE) of todo items.

Returned structure references ITodoTodo detail DTO, guaranteeing type safety and full property coverage. Errors are handled for not-found and unauthorized access cases.
operations.summary: Retrieve details of a specific todo item from todo_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Globally unique identifier (UUID) of the todo item to retrieve.

responseBody.description: A detailed todo entry and its full properties.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A todo must be created by the user (via POST /todo/user/todos) before it can be retrieved by ID. This ensures the todo exists and ownership/permissions are established in accordance with business logic and data model constraints.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item for a user within the system. It utilizes the todo_todos Prisma table, requiring a title and status property; description is optional. The operation enforces business constraints: title must be between 1 and 255 characters, description may be up to 1000 characters, and status must be either 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Ownership is established by associating the new todo item with the currently authenticated user (todo_user_id), ensuring isolated data and access. Timestamps are populated automatically per schema requirements.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item assigned to the authenticated user.

The request body must supply the todo's title (required), status (required, must be 'incomplete' or 'complete'), and (optionally) a description. The server will assign the todo_user_id based on the authenticated user. All business and validation rules for field length, allowed values, and ownership are strictly enforced and validated prior to persistence.

On success, the created todo item is returned with all persisted information, including UUID, timestamps, user ownership, and initial status. Related operations: fetching a list of todos, fetching details by id (GET /todos/{todoId}), updating (PUT), and deletion (DELETE).

Errors will be returned for invalid values, missing required fields, or authentication failures. Description of the request and response DTOs refer to strict schema naming and domain conventions.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item in todo_todos table for current user.

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new todo, enforcing title, status, and optional description, with ownership implied.

responseBody.description: Created todo item with all persisted fields including ID, timestamps, and ownership.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item in the todo_todos Prisma table. It allows an authenticated user to modify their own todo's fields, including title, description, and completion status. The specification enforces required field rules: the title must always be provided (1-255 chars), status can only be 'incomplete' or 'complete', description is optional (up to 1000 chars), and only the owner of a todo may update it. This operation also includes validation of user ownership and rejects any attempt to update a todo not belonging to the requester. Business logic ensures updated_at is always set to the current UTC time; completed_at is set only if status transitions to 'complete.' All validation and ownership checks are enforced according to the Prisma schema's constraints and comments. Hard deletes are specified at the model level, so restoration is not possible.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo item for the authenticated user.

This endpoint allows a user to update properties of their own todo entry, as defined in the todo_todos Prisma schema. The fields available for update include the title (always required), an optional description, and the completion status which must be either 'incomplete' or 'complete.'

Security is strictly enforced so only the owner (per the todo_user_id foreign key) may update their own todos. Any attempt to update another user's todo will be rejected. Timestamp management is handled as follows: the updated_at field is set automatically to the request time, and completed_at is updated if status is changed to 'complete.' All updates are atomic and fully validated against schema length and value constraints.

Business logic applies all necessary validation for title length (1-255), optional description (up to 1000 chars), and accepted status values. Attempts to use invalid status or out-of-bounds text will result in clear error messages. No multi-user sharing or delegation is possible by design. This operation references the todo_todos schema and directly incorporates its validation and security principles.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo in the todo_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to update (UUID, required).

requestBody.description: Data for updating the todo item. Fields include title (required), description (optional), and status ('incomplete' or 'complete').

responseBody.description: The updated todo item with all current fields after changes are applied.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo entry must exist before it can be updated. The POST /todo/user/todos operation is required to create a todo record, supplying the todoId used for the update operation.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a todo item from the todo_todos Prisma table. Deletion is a hard delete: the corresponding record is entirely removed from the database and cannot be restored. The operation strictly enforces user ownership—only the authenticated user who owns the todo (as indicated by the todo_user_id foreign key) is allowed to delete it. All attempts by users to delete todo items they do not own will be denied.

The operation requires the unique UUID identifier of the todo to be deleted. No request body is needed as deletion is determined solely by the path identifier and authentication context. Timestamps of deleted todos will not be retrievable after this action. All validation checks, including user ownership and identifier format, must be performed as specified in the Prisma schema and business requirements.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo item belonging to the authenticated user.

This endpoint provides hard deletion of an individual todo, as mandated by the todo_todos Prisma schema and the service's business rules. Only the user who owns the todo (per the todo_user_id foreign key) may invoke this operation. Unauthorized deletion attempts are rejected with clear errors.

No soft delete or recovery mechanism exists—deletion is absolute and cannot be undone. Upon success, the specified todo is fully purged from the database; no residual data remains accessible. This operation reflects the schema's strong stance on ownership and irreversible deletion by design. Deleted_at or similar fields do not exist—in accordance with strict deletion requirements.
operations.summary: Delete a todo from the todo_todos table (hard delete, only by owner).

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to delete (UUID, required).

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A todo entry must exist before it can be deleted. The POST /todo/user/todos operation creates a new todo and provides the todoId necessary for deletion.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoUser.ICreate.description:
User registration payload for creating a new todo_users record in the authentication system.

This schema serves as the input contract for public join (registration) API endpoints, ensuring that every user registration is validated, persisted, and securely onboarded through business rules defined in both code and the database.

All business-required fields (email, password) are included, aligning with the Prisma todo_users schema and requirements. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) exist solely for audit and advanced security analysis—they are never persisted in user records, but must be present in every registration request per system security pattern.

No implementation or system-only/authentication-properties (e.g., password hash or privileged flags) are permitted in this DTO. The schema description, field documentation, and validation rules should guide API consumers to construct well-formed registration payloads that maximize security and onboarding reliability.

email.description:
The unique email address for this user account.

Serves as a global unique identifier in the system, providing primary authentication and communication. Must satisfy RFC 5322 email constraints and is used in all user-facing business logic. Validation failures occur if the email is not unique or malformatted.

password.description:
User-supplied plaintext password, subject to minimum (8) and maximum (128) length restrictions. Plaintext is used only for this request; it is salted and hashed for storage as password_hash in the backend.

Obeys security best practices and all requirements in the system documentation. API/services must reject insufficiently strong passwords.

oneOf.description: Client's public IPv4 address, if specified, supplying extra context for session establishment and audit logging—optional and may be omitted/null.
Client's public IPv6 address, if specified, supplying extra context for session establishment and audit logging—optional and may be omitted/null.
If no client IP is provided, value MUST be null, never omitted. The server may derive IP from lower network layers or request metadata as needed.

ip.description:
Session context information for registration event.

Includes the public IP address if available (either IPv4 or IPv6 form) or null otherwise. Collected exclusively for registration event auditing, fraud detection, and security analytics. Never persisted in the todo_users table.

href.description:
The absolute URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) of the page/session from which registration was initiated.

This provides session context information that greatly enhances business reporting, fraud analysis, and traceability of user onboarding funnels. Required for all registration requests and must be directly supplied by the frontend client or calling context.

referrer.description:
The URI of the referrer page that led to the registration event.

Serves as part of the security and business context for registration analytics. Always required, must be a valid URI, and must represent the user journey accurately for traceability.

ITodoUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response body for user registration, login, and token refresh endpoints.

Contains the authenticated user's unique id and authorization token information. Returns directly after registration/join, login, and refresh operations. Uses IAuthorizationToken for token property, and also includes essential user details. This represents the initial handshake for establishing a secure session post-authentication.

Sensitive data such as password hashes are strictly excluded. Only expose secure identifier and token objects for client-side use.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user. Corresponds to todo_users.id and can be used as principal in subsequent authenticated operations.

email.description: Unique email address for the user. Used for authentication and business communication. Must be unique across all users.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the user account was first created. Used for auditing and registration analytics.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the user account (such as email or password changes).

ITodoUser.ILogin.description:
Request DTO for user login endpoint. Used for authenticating an end user against the todo_users table, issuing JWTs on successful verification. Accepts user email, password (plain text), connection context (href and referrer are required; ip is optional for system-to-system use or SSR), as described in requirements and Prisma schema.

This DTO matches authentication requirements: passwords are validated and never stored in plain text beyond checking. Session context fields are required as specified in authentication and auditing business rules. All data is single-purpose for login operations only.

Upon successful validation, the user receives JWTs. Upon failure, errors are handled generically per requirements for security.

email.description: The user's unique email address for authentication and communication. Must match the email in the todo_users table, validated against RFC 5322 standards.

password.description: Plain text user password for authentication, to be validated and securely checked. Not retained after validation; must match password_hash (hashed) in the database.

href.description: URL of the page or application context from which login is initiated. Required as part of session context to satisfy auditing flows.

referrer.description: Referrer URI from which the login action originated, used for auditing and security analytics. Must be supplied by the client.

oneOf.description: Client's IPv4 address (for session context tracking when available).
Client's IPv6 address (for session context tracking when available).
If IP is not available, set to null.

ip.description: Optional IP address of the client initiating authentication. Server may extract if not supplied; may be required for SSR or audit compliance.

ITodoUser.IRefresh.description:
Request DTO for user JWT refresh operation. Used to refresh JWT access and refresh tokens via a valid refresh token held in an active todo_user_sessions record.

The refresh token value is required; session context may be tied by lookup in the session table as per business and Prisma schema requirements. This schema supports secure token rotation for continued authorized access without repeated logins. No user credentials are retransmitted with this DTO.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token for session renewal, mapped to the todo_user_sessions record and digitally verified for validity/expiration per requirements and session schema.

ITodoUser.description:
Registered user entity for the Todo List application.

Represents an individual account in the Todo List system. All todo list data is strictly scoped by this identity. Each user is uniquely identified by their email address. Passwords are stored using cryptographic hashes only, never in plain text. No user can access or modify another user's data; strict privacy and ownership rules apply.

Timestamps indicate when the account was created and when it was most recently modified. This entity is foundational to all authentication, permission checks, and separation of user data within the system.

id.description: Universally unique identifier of the user. Serves as the primary key for identity and authentication.

email.description: Unique email address for the user. Used for authentication and business communication. Must be unique across all users.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the user account was first created. Used for auditing and registration analytics.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the user account (such as email or password changes).

ITodoUser.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating user entities in the Todo List system.

Allows filtering by email address, sorting by time fields, and full-text search features as required by administrative or analytic operations. Pagination controls are provided to restrict the number of results for efficient queries.

email.description: Filter users by exact email address. If provided, only users with this exact email are returned.

created_from.description: Filter users whose account was created on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

created_to.description: Filter users whose account was created on or before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

updated_from.description: Filter users updated on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

updated_to.description: Filter users updated on or before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

search.description: Full-text search across user email addresses for partial matches (case-insensitive).

page.description: Zero-based pagination index, starting at 1. Default is 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return in a single page. Default is 20, maximum is 100.

oneOf.description: Specifies which field to sort the user list by: email, account creation time, or last update time.
Specifies which field to sort the user list by: email, account creation time, or last update time.
Specifies which field to sort the user list by: email, account creation time, or last update time.

sort_by.description: Specifies which field to sort the user list by: email, account creation time, or last update time.

oneOf.description: Sort order for the chosen sort_by field. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).
Sort order for the chosen sort_by field. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

sort_order.description: Sort order for the chosen sort_by field. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

ITodoUser.IUpdate.description:
Data fields required to update an existing user's account information in the Todo List application.

Supports modification of email and password details according to strict schema and security requirements. Only provided fields are updated. This DTO explicitly omits id and timestamp fields, which are immutable or system-managed. The password must always be provided as plain text only; backend performs all hashing. This design reflects both best security practices and critical password field handling requirements.

Unique constraints are enforced for email, and updating the password triggers an update to the `updated_at` field at the database layer automatically. All updates are scoped to a specific user identified by the path parameter, never by data included in this DTO.

email.description: (Optional) Updated unique email address for the user. Must be unique across all users. If provided, the value is validated against email format and system uniqueness constraints.

password.description: (Optional) The new password for the user as plain text. BACKEND hashes this before storing; clients must supply ONLY plain text passwords (never pre-hashed).

ITodoUserSession.IRequest.description:
Filtering and pagination criteria for searching authentication sessions belonging to a specific user in the Todo List application.

Provides advanced search, filtering, and pagination controls to locate session records for a user. Supports querying by date ranges (created_at, expired_at), IP address, href, and referrer; and allows specification of pagination (page, limit) for result sets. The query is ALWAYS scoped to a specific user by context (path parameter), so no todo_user_id property is required. Complies fully with the subsidiary relationship specified in the schema, as well as security and auditability requirements. Designed for PATCH-based search operation in session audit endpoints.

This schema covers every legitimate client-side search constraint for session listings, excluding any creation or editing of session records.

created_at_start.description: (Optional) Lower bound for session creation timestamp (inclusive). Sessions created at or after this date-time will be included in results.

created_at_end.description: (Optional) Upper bound for session creation timestamp (inclusive). Sessions created at or before this date-time will be included in results.

expired_at_start.description: (Optional) Lower bound for session expiration timestamp. Sessions expired at or after this date-time included.

expired_at_end.description: (Optional) Upper bound for session expiration timestamp. Sessions expired at or before this date-time included.

ip.description: (Optional) IP address to filter session records for a specific login origin.

href.description: (Optional) Source URL where the session was started. Filter sessions with a specific landing or login page context.

referrer.description: (Optional) Referrer URL passed during session creation. Used to filter for sessions created from a particular referring context.

page.description: (Optional) Pagination index for session record results. Indicates which page of results to retrieve, starting from 1.

limit.description: (Optional) Page size for pagination. Number of session records to return per page. Must be a reasonable value according to business rules (typically 10-100).

id.description: Universally unique session identifier for each authentication/session instance. Primary Key as defined in the todo_user_sessions table.

todo_user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the user who owns this session. Points to todo_users.id. Establishes the parent-child relationship between session and user.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established. Used for audit and security review contexts.

href.description: Full URL where the session started (landing or login page). Used for analytics and security auditing.

referrer.description: Referrer URL for the session, providing additional context to the authentication attempt.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired, was invalidated, or logged out. Null if the session is active at present.

ITodoUserSession.description:
Authentication sessions for users of the Todo List application.

Each record represents a single authenticated session established by a user. Sessions are created at user login, persist throughout API use, and are invalidated at logout or expiration. Sessions are always linked to a specific todo_user (parent-child relationship). Fields provide connection context and timing for security and forensic analysis. Session editing and deletion are managed solely by authentication flows, not mainline business APIs.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Used to fetch designated subset of todos in search results.

limit.description: Maximum number of todo items per page (max 100). Used for paginated list responses. Defaults to standard system setting if not provided.

search.description: Text to search for in title or description fields (partial match, case-insensitive, full-text index supported if present). Optional.

oneOf.description: Optionally filters todos by completion status. Allowed values: 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Enforced to prevent unexpected consumption. Optional.
Optionally filters todos by completion status. Allowed values: 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Enforced to prevent unexpected consumption. Optional.

ITodoTodo.IRequest.description: Search and filter criteria for retrieving the user's todos. Supports filtering by completion status, text search in title/description, and custom sort/pagination options. All query behaviors match non-functional and business criteria from requirements. Ownership and authorization are strictly enforced to ensure only authenticated user's todos are accessible.

ITodoTodo.description:
Todo items for individual users.

Represents a single todo entry owned by a user. Each todo is strictly linked to its owner via a foreign key reference to todo_users. The todo includes a required title, an optional description, a status which may be 'incomplete' or 'complete', and timestamps tracking creation, last update, and (where applicable) completion. A todo cannot be shared, reassigned, or delegated to multiple users. All CRUD operations are strictly restricted to the owner. Only the owner user may view or update their own todos. Deletion is hard-delete (irreversible).

Validation rules are enforced for all fields: the title is required (1-255 chars), the description is optional (up to 1000 chars), the status is strictly an enum value ('incomplete' or 'complete'), and timestamps conform to UTC ISO8601 standards. Relationships are enforced at both the API and schema level, and no extraneous fields are accepted. Ownership is modeled through todo_user_id, but no circular user arrays exist in the user model for security and atomicity compliance.

Used as the main response schema for retrieving or updating individual todo entities.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this todo item.

title.description: Todo title. Required, must be between 1 and 255 characters as enforced by the model. Used for user display and identification.

oneOf.description: Optional extended text description. May contain up to 1000 characters; omitted or null means no description.
Description is not provided.

description.description: Optional long-form description for the todo item; up to 1000 characters, or null/omitted for none.

oneOf.description: Completion status; only allowed values are 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Enforced at all layers to prevent invalid states.
Completion status; only allowed values are 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Enforced at all layers to prevent invalid states.

status.description: Completion status; only allowed values are 'incomplete' or 'complete'. Enforced at all layers to prevent invalid states.

created_at.description: Timestamp (UTC ISO8601) when the todo was first created. Never null.

updated_at.description: Timestamp (UTC ISO8601) of the most recent modification to this todo. Always updated on change.

oneOf.description: Timestamp (UTC ISO8601) indicating when the todo transitioned to 'complete'. Null if not completed.
Not completed; therefore this field is null.

completed_at.description: Completion timestamp—only present if status is 'complete', otherwise null.

user.description: Owner user of this todo. Foreign key relation to todo_users.

ITodoTodo.ICreate.description: Data required to create a new todo item for the authenticated user. Only required and optional business fields are accepted; ownership is always set from authentication context, never from client input.

ITodoUser.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a registered user in the Todo List application.

Minimum set of identifying properties for embedding within related entities. Intended for quick lookup, ownership references, and list displays. Derived from todo_users model.

ITodoTodo.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating existing todo item fields in the todo_todos table.

Intended for use as the request body in update operations on a user's own todo entry. Permits updating of the title (1-255 chars, required), an optional description (up to 1000 chars, nullable), and completion status (enum: 'incomplete' or 'complete'). This DTO strictly omits all ownership and timestamp fields, as those are either system-generated or contextually injected, never client-supplied. Ownership (todo_user_id) and id are not updatable.

Constraints and business validation rules mirror the entity's: title cannot be empty or exceed 255 chars, description cannot exceed 1000 chars, and status must be one of the allowed values. Any attempt to alter unauthorized fields is rejected. Used exclusively for authenticated user self-updates; API enforces all length and value constraints.

Timestamps (updated_at, completed_at) and ownership enforcement occur server-side and are never supplied in this DTO.

ITodoUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary info for a single authentication session record in the Todo List application.

Represents minimal session information for audit, security UI purposes, and API responses where full session detail is not needed. Does not include sensitive data. Used for session lists, search results, and reference embedding within related entities.

Derived from the todo_user_sessions model. Belongs to a specific todo_user. Key properties include id, connection context, and relevant timestamps.

id.description: Universally unique session identifier. Used to distinguish this session for auditing and session management purposes.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established. Auditing and security use only.

href.description: Initial URL where the session started.

referrer.description: Referrer URL for the session, providing source context for the authentication attempt.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created in UTC, ISO 8601 format.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was invalidated. Null if still active.

user.description: Summary of the user who owns this session. Embedded reference to the ITodoUser.ISummary object.

ITodoTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a todo item belonging to a user.

Contains minimal identifying and status information for lists, search responses, and status widgets. Does not include full detail (such as description/body). Used as embed/reference in related entities and for light UI displays.

Derived from todo_todos model. All todos strictly belong to their user. Status indicates task completion.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item.

title.description: Todo title (1-255 characters). Required at all times.

oneOf.description: Completion status for this todo. Allowed values: 'incomplete' or 'complete'.
Completion status for this todo. Allowed values: 'incomplete' or 'complete'.

status.description: Completion status for this todo. Allowed values: 'incomplete' or 'complete'.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update, UTC, ISO 8601.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when todo was completed, or null if incomplete.

user.description: Summary of the user who owns this todo item.
